candidates.whyItFits: Iceland's second-highest waterfall at 122 meters, dropping into a dramatic canyon with basalt columns. The approach hike reveals multiple tiers and the geological story of repeated lava flows.
candidates.tradeoffs: Rough 4WD track access and weather-dependent visibility.
candidates.otherAttractions: Nearby Granni waterfall, highland driving routes, volcanic crater views

candidates.whyItFits: Waterfall framed by hexagonal basalt columns that form natural amphitheater walls. The geometric precision of the rock formations contrasts with the white water cascade.
candidates.tradeoffs: Remote highland location requiring careful route planning.
candidates.otherAttractions: Sprengisandur highland route, Hofsjokull glacier views, highland desert landscapes

candidates.whyItFits: Dramatic 454-meter mountain rising directly from black sand beaches. The jagged peaks and reflection opportunities make it a photographer's counterpoint to Stokksnes.
candidates.tradeoffs: Private land access fee required.
candidates.otherAttractions: Viking Village film set, Stokksnes peninsula walks, seal watching

candidates.whyItFits: Iceland's northernmost mainland town, positioned for optimal northern lights viewing with minimal light pollution. The Arctic Henge stone circle adds a modern mystical element.
candidates.tradeoffs: Very limited services and dining options.
candidates.otherAttractions: Arctic Henge monument, Melrakkasletta peninsula, puffin colonies at Raudinupur

candidates.whyItFits: Serpentine canyon carved by glacial meltwater over 9,000 years. The walking path along the rim reveals the canyon's curves and the river's persistence in shaping basalt.
candidates.tradeoffs: Can be crowded during peak season due to social media popularity.
candidates.otherAttractions: Kirkjubaejarklaustur town, Systrafoss waterfall, Dverghamrar basalt columns

candidates.whyItFits: Iceland's third-highest waterfall at 128 meters, distinguished by red clay stripes in the cliff face that mark ancient volcanic eruptions. The 2.5km hike passes smaller Litlanesfoss with its basalt column frame.
candidates.tradeoffs: Moderate uphill hike required in potentially muddy conditions.
candidates.otherAttractions: Litlanesfoss waterfall, Lagarfljot lake, Hallormsstadaskogur forest

candidates.whyItFits: Strategic ring road town where the Blanda river meets the sea. The textile museum occupies a 1896 building and tells the story of Icelandic wool processing through original machinery.
candidates.tradeoffs: Limited evening entertainment options.
candidates.otherAttractions: Textile Museum, Blanda river salmon fishing, Vatnsnes peninsula seal colonies

candidates.whyItFits: Series of waterfalls emerging directly from a lava field over 900 meters. The water filters through porous rock for decades before appearing as springs, creating an unusual geological display.
candidates.tradeoffs: Can feel less dramatic than single-drop waterfalls.
candidates.otherAttractions: Barnafoss rapids, Deildartunguhver hot spring, Reykholt historical site

candidates.whyItFits: Waterfall within Thingvellir National Park where the Oxara river was diverted in 930 AD to supply the world's first parliament. The falls demonstrate how Icelanders shaped their landscape for governance.
candidates.tradeoffs: Often crowded due to Golden Circle tour inclusion.
candidates.otherAttractions: Thingvellir parliament site, Silfra diving fissure, continental drift viewing

candidates.whyItFits: Glass dome observatory built on geothermal tanks offers 360-degree views of Reykjavik and surrounding volcanic landscape, with planetarium showing aurora displays when weather doesn't cooperate.
candidates.tradeoffs: Tourist-focused presentation rather than raw landscape experience.

candidates.whyItFits: Small lava cave with geothermal hot spring, formed during the 1975-1984 Krafla volcanic episodes - shows how recent geological activity shapes the landscape you're driving through.
candidates.tradeoffs: Water too hot for bathing since volcanic activity increased temperatures.

candidates.whyItFits: Serpentine canyon carved 100 meters deep through palagonite rock over 9,000 years - shows how glacial meltwater shapes volcanic terrain.
candidates.tradeoffs: Popular spot with limited parking during peak season.

candidates.whyItFits: Cinder cone formed during the 1973 eruption that nearly destroyed the town - you can walk to the crater rim and see where lava flows stopped just short of the harbor.
candidates.tradeoffs: Ground still warm in places, requires sturdy footwear.

candidates.whyItFits: Multi-tiered waterfall dropping through narrow gorge just outside town - less visited alternative that shows the same glacial carving forces as larger falls.
candidates.tradeoffs: Short but steep approach trail can be slippery when wet.

candidates.whyItFits: Series of cascades where Botnsá river cuts through lava field - accessible example of how water carves through different volcanic rock layers.
candidates.tradeoffs: Smaller scale than major waterfalls on your route.

candidates.whyItFits: Blue waterfall cascading through black lava rock formations, creating an otherworldly color contrast that complements the golden falls nearby.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires a 3km hike on unmarked trails that can be muddy.

candidates.whyItFits: Hidden waterfall behind a narrow rock crevice, accessible by wading through shallow water - the geological opposite of its famous neighbor.
candidates.tradeoffs: You will get soaked from spray and stream crossing.

candidates.whyItFits: Narrow waterfall you can walk behind completely, offering the behind-the-falls experience that Skogafoss promises but doesn't quite deliver.
candidates.tradeoffs: Easy to miss - no signage and requires walking past Skogafoss parking area.

candidates.whyItFits: Horseshoe-shaped waterfall upstream from Dettifoss, demonstrating how the Jokulsa a Fjollum river carved this entire canyon system.
candidates.tradeoffs: Often overshadowed by its more powerful neighbor downstream.

candidates.whyItFits: Smaller glacial lagoon with closer iceberg access and fewer crowds, fed by the same Vatnajokull glacier system.
candidates.tradeoffs: Less dramatic scale and fewer seals than its famous neighbor.

candidates.whyItFits: Waterfall surrounded by dark basalt columns that inspired Reykjavik's Hallgrimskirkja church design, accessible via hiking trail from the park.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires 3km round-trip hike with some elevation gain.

candidates.whyItFits: Red crater lake formed in 1477 eruption, accessible via 45-minute hike from Landmannalaugar parking area with striking color contrast against black volcanic slopes.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires additional hiking time when you're already in a hiking-intensive area.

candidates.whyItFits: Two-tiered waterfall cutting through the edge of the Eldhraun lava field, showing the interaction between water and the 1783 volcanic landscape.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires 4WD vehicle and river crossing to reach.

candidates.whyItFits: Active lava field from 1975-1984 eruptions with steaming ground and sulfur deposits, accessible via marked trail from Krafla parking area.
candidates.tradeoffs: Ground can be unstable and hot in places requiring careful footing.

candidates.whyItFits: Deep lake on Reykjanes Peninsula that lost 20% of its water after 2000 earthquakes opened fissures in the lake bed, creating an otherworldly landscape.
candidates.tradeoffs: Can be windy and desolate feeling compared to more dramatic sights.

candidates.whyItFits: Small lava cave with geothermal hot spring, historically used for bathing until volcanic activity made it too hot, now accessible for viewing.
candidates.tradeoffs: Water too hot for bathing and cave space is quite small.

candidates.whyItFits: Waterfall along the Varmá river system feeding into Reykjadalur valley, accessible via short detour from the main geothermal hiking trail.
candidates.tradeoffs: Less dramatic than major waterfalls and requires extra hiking time.

candidates.whyItFits: Natural rock arch and promontory offering elevated views over Reynisfjara black beach and the Reynisdrangar sea stacks from above.
candidates.tradeoffs: Can be closed during puffin nesting season (May-August).

candidates.whyItFits: Twin basalt sea stacks rising 75 meters from the ocean, remnants of a volcanic crater wall that showcase the peninsula's volcanic origins.
candidates.tradeoffs: Strong winds make the clifftop viewing area uncomfortable in bad weather.

candidates.whyItFits: A narrow ravine you can walk into for several hundred meters, carved by glacial meltwater and mentioned in Bárðar saga as a giant's throwing spot.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires scrambling over wet rocks and can be impassable in winter.

candidates.whyItFits: Iceland's most reliable seal watching beach where harbor seals haul out year-round on the golden sand and rocky outcrops.
candidates.tradeoffs: Seals are easily disturbed and will flee if approached too closely.

candidates.whyItFits: Coastal village with dramatic basalt cliff formations and natural arches carved by Atlantic storms, plus the Bárður Snæfellsás statue overlooking the sea.
candidates.tradeoffs: Limited facilities and can be completely socked in by fog.

candidates.whyItFits: A 30-meter waterfall that drops directly into the sea near Djupivogur, accessible by a short hike along the coastline.
candidates.tradeoffs: Rough gravel road access and no marked trail to the viewpoint.

candidates.whyItFits: Small island accessible by boat from Djupivogur harbor, home to thousands of puffins in summer and the oldest wooden church in Iceland from 1807.
candidates.tradeoffs: Boat trips are weather dependent and only run June through August.

candidates.whyItFits: Horseshoe-shaped canyon 3.5 km long carved by glacial floods, with hiking trails through birch forest and views from the rim.
candidates.tradeoffs: The full rim hike takes 3-4 hours and can be muddy after rain.

candidates.whyItFits: Uninhabited peninsula accessible only by boat from Isafjordur, with arctic fox populations and dramatic cliff scenery at Iceland's northernmost point.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires a full day boat trip and hiking in potentially harsh weather conditions.

candidates.whyItFits: Small island in Isafjordur bay accessible by boat, home to thousands of eider ducks and puffins, plus Iceland's smallest post office.
candidates.tradeoffs: Boat schedule is limited and trips can be cancelled due to weather.

candidates.whyItFits: Small island connected to Stykkisholmur by a causeway, topped with a lighthouse and offering panoramic views over Breidafjordur bay.
candidates.tradeoffs: The walk up is steep and can be slippery when wet.

candidates.whyItFits: Family-run museum and working shark processing facility where you can learn about traditional hákarl production and taste fermented shark.
candidates.tradeoffs: The smell is overwhelming and the taste of hákarl is notoriously challenging.

candidates.whyItFits: Natural hot river where you can soak in geothermal waters after a 3km hike through steaming valleys - more authentic than constructed pools.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires moderate hiking and weather can change quickly in the valley.

candidates.whyItFits: 3000-year-old volcanic crater with turquoise lake - compact example of Iceland's volcanic formation visible from rim walk.
candidates.tradeoffs: Small entrance fee and can be crowded during peak hours.

candidates.whyItFits: Brilliant blue waterfall cascading over dark lava rock - striking color contrast from glacial minerals in a more intimate setting.
candidates.tradeoffs: Requires 2km walk from parking and path can be muddy.

placeActivities.name: Place to stay overnight
placeActivities.description: Cities and towns you flagged as overnight stays. These anchor the trip's geography — they're where you sleep and the bases for day trips.

placeActivities.name: Drive the complete Ring Road counterclockwise
placeActivities.description: Iceland's Route 1 circles the entire island through volcanic landscapes, black sand beaches, and dramatic coastlines.

placeActivities.name: Catch the Northern Lights
placeActivities.description: Aurora borealis appears on clear, dark nights from September through March across Iceland's countryside.
placeActivities.conditionNote: Clear skies and minimal light pollution required for visibility.

placeActivities.name: Visit the major waterfalls
placeActivities.description: Iceland's waterfalls range from the powerful Gullfoss to the curtain-like Seljalandsfoss where you can walk behind the cascade.

placeActivities.name: Explore glacial lagoons and icebergs
placeActivities.description: Jokulsarlon lagoon holds icebergs calved from Vatnajokull glacier, while nearby Diamond Beach displays ice chunks on black volcanic sand.

placeActivities.name: Walk on glaciers and ice caves
placeActivities.section: Walk on ice and volcanic terrain
placeActivities.description: Guided glacier walks on Vatnajokull and seasonal ice cave tours reveal the interior structure of Europe's largest glacier.

placeActivities.name: Hike to volcanic craters and lava fields
placeActivities.section: Walk on ice and volcanic terrain
placeActivities.description: Active volcanic zones like Landmannalaugar offer colorful rhyolite mountains, while Eldhraun lava field shows the scale of historical eruptions.

placeActivities.name: Soak in geothermal hot springs
placeActivities.description: Natural hot springs range from the developed Blue Lagoon to remote pools like Reykjadalur valley where you hike to reach the water.

placeActivities.name: See black sand beaches and sea stacks
placeActivities.description: Reynisfjara beach near Vik displays basalt columns and offshore sea stacks, while Stokksnes offers views of Vestrahorn mountain.

placeActivities.name: Explore Reykjavik's culture and nightlife
placeActivities.description: Iceland's capital holds the National Museum, Hallgrimskirkja church, and a concentrated music and bar scene along Laugavegur street.

placeActivities.name: Taste Icelandic seafood and traditional foods
placeActivities.description: Fresh langoustine, Arctic char, and traditional preparations like fermented shark represent Iceland's fishing culture and preservation methods.

placeActivities.name: Visit the Westman Islands
placeActivities.description: Heimaey island holds the world's largest puffin colony and shows recent volcanic activity from the 1973 Eldfell eruption.

placeActivities.name: Drive the Snaefellsnes Peninsula
placeActivities.description: The peninsula concentrates Iceland's landscapes in miniature: Snaefellsjokull glacier, Kirkjufell mountain, and fishing villages like Arnarstapi.

placeActivities.name: Explore the East Fjords fishing villages
placeActivities.description: Remote fjord towns like Seydisfjordur and Djupivogur preserve traditional fishing culture and offer access to hiking trails.

placeActivities.name: This trip is tight on time
placeActivities.description: A complete Ring Road circuit with Northern Lights viewing requires 3+ nights in multiple bases for aurora chances. Consider 25-30 days for a comfortable pace, or focus on either the full ring OR extended aurora viewing.

placeActivities.name: Visit Husavik
placeActivities.description: Primary whale watching hub on the north coast with excellent northern lights viewing.

placeActivities.name: Visit Isafjordur
placeActivities.description: Largest town in the remote Westfjords with dramatic fjord setting and historic architecture.

placeActivities.name: Visit Stykkisholmur
placeActivities.description: Historic fishing town on Snaefellsnes Peninsula and gateway to Breidafjordur islands.

placeActivities.name: Visit Hveragerdi
placeActivities.description: Geothermal town south of Reykjavik known as Iceland's greenhouse capital with hot spring hiking.

placeActivities.name: Visit Selfoss
placeActivities.description: Largest town in southern Iceland and practical base for Golden Circle exploration.

placeActivities.name: Max-suggested additions, in the shape of your list
placeActivities.description: Max read your existing picks as a signal of taste and added these. Check the ones that fit; ignore the rest.

placeActivities.name: Near-by enrichment
placeActivities.description: Nearby sights and activities tied to the places already in your Discovery. Each one is anchored to a place you've listed.
